subject: music
topicDisplay: Component 1 Listening Western And World Music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The 'basso continuo', a continuous bass line often played by harpsichord and cello, is a feature of which period?
questions.explain: The basso continuo is a defining feature of Baroque music.

questions.q: A fugue is a piece based on:
options: Imitative counterpoint built from a subject
questions.explain: A fugue develops a main theme (subject) through imitative entries in different voices.
The djembe is a West African goblet-shaped hand drum.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the rhythmic cycle is known as the:
questions.explain: The tala is the repeating rhythmic cycle, while the raga is the melodic framework.

questions.q: A recurring musical theme linked to a character, place or idea in film or opera is a:
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme associated with a character, place or idea.

questions.q: Which of these is a string instrument of the orchestra?
questions.explain: The cello belongs to the string family; clarinet is woodwind and trumpet is brass.

questions.q: Which instrument is most associated with traditional Irish folk music?
questions.explain: The tin whistle and fiddle are staples of traditional Irish folk music.

questions.q: Romantic music (c1810-1910) is generally noted for:
options: Strong emotional expression and large orchestras
questions.explain: Romantic music emphasises emotion, expression and often larger orchestras.

questions.q: Which composer is most associated with the Baroque period?
questions.explain: J.S. Bach is a leading Baroque composer; Beethoven bridged Classical and Romantic.

options: Blends elements of two or more musical styles
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more different musical styles or traditions.
The Baroque period (c1600-1750) came before the Classical period.

questions.q: Roughly which dates define the Classical period?
questions.explain: The Classical period spans roughly 1750 to 1820.
